name: Two-phase liquid-argon ionization and scintillation detection at 87 K
plain_name: Two-phase liquid-argon ionization and scintillation detection at 87 K
description: Detect particle interactions through prompt VUV scintillation and an electron signal extracted across a liquid-gas argon boundary, as in the 2.3 litre WARP prototype.

sources.citation: Benetti et al., First results from a Dark Matter search with liquid Argon at 87 K

requirements.rationale: The reported liquid-argon target is at 87 K.
The detector needs drift/extraction electrodes and VUV readout, not simply liquid argon cooling.

missing_information: Argon purity, electron lifetime, HV field, extraction efficiency and backgrounds are not quantified in this bounded profile; no dark-matter discrimination or sensitivity claim follows from passing it.
confirmation_note: Curated bounded procedure from the cited source. User must confirm applicability before an interactive verification. Passing encoded checks does not establish unmodeled performance.
verification_scope: Temperature plus the named indispensable measurement/handling functions; no extrapolation of undocumented performance, pressure, calibration, cleanliness or full facility safety.
